reason: The goal asks what the lane-born stars do in the returning galaxy, so its stellar outskirts are the natural encounter site.

choice.combine: Young stars from the dark lane
choice.with: Stellar outskirts of the returning galaxy

expectation: The stars will pass through the returning galaxy's stellar outskirts, with their paths altered by gravity.

effect: The stars passed through the returning galaxy without colliding like their parent gas, completing the chapter's goal.
reaction: The contrast between the gas collision and the stars' passage was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Sending the lane-born stars through the returning galaxy was worthwhile because it showed how the same material behaves differently after becoming stars.

leastWorthwhile.text: The chapter was very short, so there was little opportunity to explore the other visible hotspot.

surprise.text: The result emphasized that the stars' paths join a shared stellar body without the stars crushing together.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary; the destination followed directly from the goal.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the shared galaxy develops, though this chapter alone offered only one brief decision.
